card.name: Words just before incidence percentages
card.fires_on: Verbs and linking words right after an adverse event is named, just before the rate is given, such as 'occurred', 'was observed', 'at' or 'within'. It appears in clinical-trial results sentences.

modes.label: Occurred before a rate
modes.description: The verb or preposition after an adverse event, right before a percentage or timing.
modes.example: In LITESPARK-022, hypoxia<< occurred>> in 7% of patients receiving W

modes.label: At or within after event
modes.description: Prepositions such as 'at' or 'within' after an event, leading into a rate or time point.
modes.example: SARs occurred<< at>> the first administration in 1.9

modes.label: Event noun before the figure
modes.description: The event term itself, such as vomiting or a lab value, right before the frequency statement.

card.writes: It suppresses words meaning 'majority' and 'most', so the text is less likely to move on to a 'most patients' phrase.
card.plain: It fires on the small words that come right after a side effect is named and just before the sentence says how often it happened.
